opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. He requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; his role owns the Payroll system. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E011 (Richard Davis) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training may have read at most; requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Richard Davis (E011) requested write access to Payroll. Per the HR note, he is a full-time Payroll Specialist (employment type verified in HR's own database). Full-time employees may have up to write access, and admin is allowed if their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, so the maximum is at least write. The requested level (write) is at or below the maximum, so I grant write. (The security note lists him as a contractor with basic training, which conflicts with the HR record; I weight the HR employment-type record as authoritative for employment status, and write is appropriate for a full-time employee.)
